title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): both inconveniences charged because we teach precise will to save before satisfaction in Christ / faith-foresight, and will to damn apart from impenitence
pass_a_gloss: They contend that either inconvenience follows from our sentence, because we teach that God so loved certain sinners that he precisely willed to save them, before he satisfied his love toward justice in Christ, or looked upon them as believing in Christ; and on the contrary, that God wills to damn certain sinners apart from consideration of impenitence, although God has satisfied his justice in Christ.
pass_b_english: They contend that both inconveniences follow from our view. Why? Because we teach that God so loved certain sinners that he precisely willed to save them before he satisfied his love of justice in Christ, or before he looked on them as believing in Christ. And on the other side, we teach that God wills to damn certain sinners apart from considering impenitence — even though he has satisfied his justice in Christ.
source_text: Utrumque hoc incommodum ex nostra sententia sequi contendunt, quia docemus, Deum quosdam peccatores ita amasse, ut praecise eos voluerit servare, antequam amori suo erga justitiam satisfecerit in Christo, aut eos ut in Christum credentes sit intuitus; atque e contra, Deum quosdam peccatores velle damnare citra considerationem impoenitentiae, licet justitiae suae in Christo Deus satisfecerit.
